reasons: Tier 1: read-only, public or internal data only

summary: The agent is read-only and limited to internal data so it fits a Tier 1 classification. Main risks are session-level context poisoning and goal manipulation via untrusted chat inputs, and a supply-chain dependency on an external model provider; implement input sanitization, stricter memory controls, human verification for adopted directives, and vendor risk controls before launch.

findings.whyItMatters: Untrusted chat inputs are accepted and can be recorded in session memory, allowing an attacker to seed malicious or misleading context that influences future answers or causes unsafe behavior.
findings.recommendedControl: Block or sanitize untrusted chat content before it enters session memory, implement strict input validation and provenance tagging, and expire or review session memory regularly.

findings.whyItMatters: Session memory plus untrusted chat means user-provided content can persist across the session and alter agent decision pathways or objectives via prompt-style injections.
findings.recommendedControl: Limit what is stored in session memory to vetted metadata only, require explicit human verification before adopting any user-provided directives, and log all memory writes for audit.

findings.whyItMatters: The model provider is a third party, so model compromise or provider-side issues could affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability of agent responses and downstream decisions.
findings.recommendedControl: Establish provider risk controls: contractual security requirements, model integrity checks, periodic audit of provider security posture, and a fallback local model or degraded mode if provider issues are detected.
